s: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
fakta: A year on Mercury lasts only 88 Earth days.

s: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
fakta: Mars is red because its soil is full of rusty iron.

s: What is the largest planet in our solar system?
fakta: More than 1,300 Earths could fit inside Jupiter.

s: Which planet has the most famous rings?
fakta: Saturn's rings are made of ice and rock.

s: What gas do plants take in from the air?
fakta: Plants give off oxygen as they make food from sunlight.

s: At what temperature does water freeze?
fakta: Salt water freezes at a lower temperature than fresh water.

s: At what temperature does water boil at sea level?
fakta: High up a mountain, water boils at a lower temperature.

s: How many planets are in our solar system?
fakta: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.

s: What is the name of our galaxy?
fakta: The Milky Way has hundreds of billions of stars.

s: What does a thermometer measure?
fakta: Air pressure is measured with a barometer.

s: What is H2O better known as?
fakta: Each water molecule has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

s: Which organ pumps blood around the body?
fakta: An adult heart beats around 100,000 times a day.

s: How many bones are in an adult human body?
fakta: A baby is born with around 300 bones, and some of them grow together.

s: What is the hardest natural substance?
fakta: Diamond is made of pure carbon, like the graphite in a pencil.

s: What is the closest star to Earth?
fakta: Light from the Sun takes about eight minutes to reach us.

s: Which part of the body has the smallest bone?
fakta: The stirrup bone in the middle ear is about 3 millimetres long.

s: What force keeps us on the ground?
fakta: On the Moon you would weigh about a sixth of what you do on Earth.

s: What do bees, butterflies and the wind help plants to do?
fakta: Without pollination many fruits would never form.

s: What is the largest organ of the human body?
fakta: An adult's skin weighs around 4 kg.

s: What colour do you get by mixing blue and yellow paint?
fakta: Red, yellow and blue are the primary colours in painting.

s: How many colours are in a rainbow?
fakta: Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.

s: What is the Moon's pull on the sea responsible for?
fakta: There are usually two high tides a day.

s: Which planet spins on its side?
fakta: Uranus may have been knocked over by a huge collision long ago.

s: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
fakta: Au comes from the Latin word ‘aurum’.

s: What is the chemical symbol for iron?
fakta: Fe comes from the Latin word ‘ferrum’.

s: What is the most common gas in the air we breathe?
fakta: About 78 per cent of the air is nitrogen.

s: Which British scientist described gravity after, legend says, an apple fell?
fakta: Newton's apple tree still grows at Woolsthorpe Manor in Lincolnshire.

s: Who wrote ‘On the Origin of Species’ in 1859?
fakta: Darwin's ideas about evolution were shaped by his visit to the Galápagos Islands.

s: Who discovered penicillin in 1928?
fakta: Fleming noticed that mould had killed bacteria on a dish he had left out.

s: Who made the first vaccine, against smallpox, in 1796?
fakta: The word ‘vaccine’ comes from the Latin for cow, after cowpox.

s: Which planet is the hottest in our solar system?
fakta: Venus's thick clouds trap heat, making it hotter than Mercury.

s: What is the speed of light, roughly?
fakta: Light could go around the Earth about seven times in one second.

s: What is the centre of an atom called?
fakta: The nucleus holds protons and neutrons.

s: What kind of animal was Dolly, the first cloned mammal?
fakta: Dolly was born in Scotland in 1996.

s: Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart?
fakta: Veins carry blood back to the heart.

s: What is the name of the force that slows a sliding object?
fakta: Without friction it would be impossible to walk.

s: What is the boiling point of water in Fahrenheit?
fakta: Water freezes at 32 °F.

s: Which planet has a Great Red Spot?
fakta: The Great Red Spot is a giant storm that has raged for at least 150 years.

s: How long does the Earth take to go once around the Sun?
fakta: That is why we add a leap day every four years.

s: What do we call a scientist who studies rocks?
fakta: A botanist studies plants.

s: Which scientist is famous for E = mc²?
fakta: Einstein won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921.

s: What is the name of the telescope launched into space in 1990?
fakta: Hubble has made more than a million observations.

s: Which scientist was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize?
fakta: Marie Curie won two Nobel Prizes, in physics and chemistry.

s: What is the name for animals with a backbone?
fakta: Insects and worms are invertebrates.

s: How many teeth does an adult usually have?
fakta: That includes four wisdom teeth, which not everyone gets.

s: What is the largest moon of Saturn?
fakta: Titan has rivers and lakes of liquid methane.

s: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
fakta: Mercury was once used in thermometers.

s: Which vitamin does the skin make in sunlight?
fakta: In the dark British winter, many people take vitamin D supplements.

s: What is the study of the weather called?
fakta: The Met Office in Exeter gives Britain's official forecasts.

s: What do red blood cells carry around the body?
fakta: They get their red colour from iron in haemoglobin.

s: Who is known as the first computer programmer?
fakta: She wrote about Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine in the 1840s.

s: Which British mathematician helped crack the Enigma code at Bletchley Park?
fakta: Turing also laid the foundations of computer science.

s: Who invented the World Wide Web?
fakta: He wrote the plan for the web at CERN in 1989.

s: Which scientist discovered electromagnetic induction in 1831?
fakta: Faraday's discovery made electric generators possible.

s: Which Scottish engineer improved the steam engine in the 1700s?
fakta: The watt, a unit of power, is named after him.

s: Which Scot showed the first working television in 1926?
fakta: Baird gave the demonstration in Soho, London.

s: What is the most abundant element in the universe?
fakta: Stars like the Sun are mostly hydrogen.

s: What is the chemical symbol for sodium?
fakta: Na comes from the Latin ‘natrium’.

s: How long does light from the Sun take to reach Earth?
fakta: The Sun is about 150 million km away.

s: What is absolute zero in degrees Celsius?
fakta: Nothing can be colder than absolute zero.

s: Which scientist's photograph helped reveal the double helix of DNA?
fakta: Photo 51 was taken in her laboratory at King's College London in 1952.

s: What is the name of the boundary around a black hole beyond which nothing can escape?
fakta: Not even light can escape once past the event horizon.

s: How many chromosomes are in a normal human body cell?
fakta: Egg and sperm cells have 23 each.

s: Which gas makes up most of the Sun?
fakta: In the Sun's core, hydrogen is fused into helium.

s: What is the scientific name for the kneecap?
fakta: The femur, in the thigh, is the longest bone in the body.

s: Which unit is used to measure electrical resistance?
fakta: It is named after the German scientist Georg Ohm.

s: What is the closest large galaxy to the Milky Way?
fakta: Andromeda is about 2.5 million light years away, yet you can see it without a telescope.

s: Which element has the chemical symbol K?
fakta: K comes from the Latin word ‘kalium’.

s: Which British astronomer discovered Uranus in 1781?
fakta: Herschel wanted to name the planet after King George III.

s: Which comet returns about every 76 years?
fakta: It was last seen from Earth in 1986 and is due back in 2061.

s: Which part of the brain controls balance?
fakta: The word cerebellum means ‘little brain’ in Latin.

s: What is the name of the largest volcano in the solar system, on Mars?
fakta: Olympus Mons is about two and a half times as tall as Mount Everest.

s: What is the pH of pure water?
fakta: Acids have a pH below 7 and alkalis above 7.

s: Which British physicist wrote ‘A Brief History of Time’?
fakta: Hawking studied black holes and held Newton's old chair at Cambridge.

s: Who was the first British astronaut to go into space?
fakta: Helen Sharman flew to the Mir space station in 1991.

s: What is the name of the force that holds planets in orbit around the Sun?
fakta: Newton showed that the same force makes apples fall and keeps the Moon in orbit.

s: What do we call a person who travels into space?
fakta: Russian space travellers are called cosmonauts.

s: Which of these does a magnet attract?
fakta: The Earth itself behaves like a giant magnet, which is why compasses work.

s: Which organs do we use to breathe?
fakta: An adult's lungs can hold around six litres of air.
